text:
Alex Cortez: Quick sync: ACME POC sizing — they want to commit 24/7 reserved capacity with burst to handle seasonal traffic. Need recommended reserved GPU count, autoscale policy, and an estimated monthly cost delta vs hosted. Also any blockers from security questionnaire. cc @Maria @Duncan @Lina
Maria Nguyen: quick q — what's their steady req/s, peak burst, and p95 latency target? avg tokens per request?
Alex Cortez: Baseline: ~30 req/s steady, peaks up to ~120 req/s for 5–10m. Target p95 <= 300ms. Avg prompt+generation ~1200 tokens. Expect KV cache hit ~30%.
Duncan Patel: For that profile on A100-80GB equiv: 4 reserved GPUs gives ~40–50 steady req/s depending on batching. For peaks to 120 req/s we recommend reserved=6 plus burst credits / 2 on-demand GPUs for safety. Autoscale: scale-up at 75% gpu util, scale-down after 10m idle. Prewarm before business hours.
Lina Chen: On the app side: plan a canary day1 and a fallback route to a quantized 8-bit model for extreme load. Prefix/KV cache will cut token work — call that out in the SOW. We'll add a dedicated low-latency route for customer-facing flows.
Samir Rao: Rough cost sketch: reserved GPU unit price $3,200/mo (example benchmark). 6 reserved -> $19,200/mo. On-demand burst ~ $0.60/min/gpu -> estimate monthly burst $700–1,100 depending on usage. Network + infra add ~$1k. I'll run a more precise calc.
Maria Nguyen: Operational concern: if sustained 120 req/s with 1200 tokens each, latency spikes. Need request queueing + rejection policy. Recommend soft queue cap ~300 concurrent requests, then 429 + upstream retry hints. Add SLIs for token-level latency and queue length.
Alex Cortez: They asked about SLA 99.9 and AZ failover — can we cover that with reserved?
Duncan Patel: Reserved capacity is per-AZ. Recommend two-AZ layout: primary pool (4 GPUs) + warm secondary (2 GPUs) in another AZ for failover. On failover, warm pool can take traffic with small perf hit. Add prewarm job to keep KV cache hot in secondary.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: prewarm job scheduled: acme-prewarm-1 -> runs daily 03:00 UTC :gear:
security-bot: security-bot: questionnaire notes — they require KMS integration for key separation + audit logs retention 1yr. If they need isolated control plane or on‑prem, recommend Private deployment. Dedicated (VPC) works if they accept network peering and HSM options.
Lina Chen: For the POC I'd propose a 90-day reserved commit (convert option to Dedicated later). SOW will include canary, rollback, and an operator runbook covering AZ failover and burst scenarios.
Alex Cortez: Action items: @Samir send provisional pricing by EOD; @Duncan write autoscale + AZ plan; @Maria outline runbook and SLIs; @Lina draft the POC SOW. Thanks! :thumbsup:
Samir Rao: On it. I'll include a delta table: reserved vs hosted (per-token amortized) and savings if they accept 8-bit quantized models.
Duncan Patel: One more ask — add a circuit-breaker to route to hosted API if private/dedicated capacity exhausted. More expensive but keeps app online and meets SLA.
Alex Cortez: Perfect. I'll consolidate into the customer-facing doc once we have the pricing and the runbook snippets.
Maria Nguyen: I'll also stub the 429/retry guidance and an emergency scale runbook (manual scale play).
Lina Chen: I'll draft SOW + failure runbook and share for review.
